findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: docs/parallel-decomposition-spec.md line 372 still defines resolveParallelGate as a one-parameter helper (raw?: unknown): ParallelGateConfig, but the implementation in audit-config.ts exports a two-parameter form resolveParallelGate(raw: unknown, profileDefault: ParallelGateConfig). The spec was not updated to match the OQ-001 decision. Any caller reading the spec will write code that omits profileDefault and gets a TypeScript error or runtime misbehavior.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED: docs/parallel-decomposition-spec.md §4.7 now documents the two-param resolveParallelGate(raw: unknown, profileDefault: ParallelGateConfig) signature (updated rounds 2-3); round-6 docs/concept lanes confirmed spec matches impl.

findings.desc: CHK-001:happy:0: intent claims resolveParallelGate is called with lightDefault as the profileDefault, but the smoke (line 60-63 of parallel-gate-config-smoke.ts) uses PD which is the balanced default (advise/3/false). The evidence note repeats the intent wording verbatim without reflecting what the code actually does. The intent is covered by a real assertion but with a different profileDefault than stated.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED: smoke rewritten to LIGHT/BALANCED/STRICT consts (no shared 'PD'); CHK-001:happy:0 covered by 'valid full override applied' + per-profile default cases 1, each binding the named profile default.

findings.desc: CHK-001:happy:4: intent claims the smoke verifies a full return {mode:"off",maxConcurrentReview:3,broadGlobBlocks:false} but the smoke (line 66) only checks that the returned mode field equals "off". The maxConcurrentReview and broadGlobBlocks values of the return are never asserted. The intent’s concrete return-value claim is only partially covered.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED: case 'mode off accepted (full return)' asserts eq(resolveParallelGate({mode:'off'},BALANCED), {mode:'off',maxConcurrentReview:3,broadGlobBlocks:false}) — full return value, not just .mode.

findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:3: intent claims resolveParallelGate({maxConcurrentReview:2.5}, strictDefault) -> returns 4 (the strict profile default). The smoke (line 78) uses PD (balanced default, maxConcurrentReview=3) and therefore asserts the return is 3, not 4. The intent names strictDefault and the value 4 but the actual assertion uses a different profile entirely. This specific named-profile behavior is untested.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED: expectMaxFallback(2.5, STRICT, 4, 'float-strict') asserts a non-integer max falls back to the STRICT profile default 4 (the profile the intent names).

findings.desc: CHK-001:adversarial:0: intent claims resolveParallelGate("not-an-object", lightDefault) -> returns full lightDefault. The smoke (line 54) uses PD (balanced default, advise/3/false) not lightDefault (advise/2/false). The intent asserts a specific profile by name; the actual test uses a different profile. The distinction matters because lightDefault has maxConcurrentReview=2 and the claim that it returns the light values cannot be verified from this assertion.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED: 'string raw -> light default' asserts eq(resolveParallelGate('nope', LIGHT), LIGHT) — non-object yields the full LIGHT default named by the intent.

findings.desc: parallel-gate-config-smoke.ts:126 empty catch {} in finally cleanup swallows rmSync errors silently; add at least a console.warn to surface unexpected temp-dir cleanup failures during CI runs
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED: the finally cleanup catch now console.warns '[parallel-gate-config-smoke] temp cleanup failed ...' instead of swallowing rmSync errors.

findings.desc: CHK-001:adversarial:2: intent claims resolveParallelGate(null, strictDefault) -> returns full strictDefault ({block,4,true}). The smoke (line 53) uses PD (balanced default, advise/3/false). The intent names strictDefault and implies the full strict values are returned; the actual assertion only proves null -> balanced default. The strict-profile variant of this guard is never exercised.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED: 'null raw -> strict default' asserts eq(resolveParallelGate(null, STRICT), STRICT) — full strict default.

findings.desc: CHK-001:adversarial:3: intent claims the input is resolveParallelGate({mode:123,maxConcurrentReview:"abc",broadGlobBlocks:99}, balancedDefault) with mode as a number (123). The smoke (line 92-95) uses {mode:"bad",maxConcurrentReview:"x",broadGlobBlocks:1} with mode as a string ("bad"). A string mode hits the VALID_PARALLEL_MODES check path; a numeric mode may hit a typeof guard or toString path differently. The specific numeric-mode input named in the intent is not tested.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED: 'numeric (present non-string) mode -> advise, NEVER block' uses {mode:123} under STRICT and asserts mode==='advise' + a warn.

findings.desc: CHK-001:adversarial:4: intent claims resolveParallelGate({maxConcurrentReview:Infinity}, lightDefault) -> falls back to profile default 2. The smoke (line 79) uses PD (balanced default, maxConcurrentReview=3) and asserts the return is 3 not 2. The intent names lightDefault and the fallback value 2; the actual assertion uses balanced and returns 3. The light-profile variant of Infinity rejection is untested.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED: expectMaxFallback(Infinity, LIGHT, 2, 'Infinity') asserts maxConcurrentReview Infinity falls back to the LIGHT profile default 2.

findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:0 and CHK-002:edge:0: both intents claim the smoke verifies that a warn is emitted to console when an invalid mode is supplied. The smoke never captures or asserts on console.warn output (no spy, no mock, no stderr capture). The warn side-effect is visible in the validate run output only because audit-config.ts calls console.warn unconditionally; the smoke does not include any assertion that the warning was actually emitted. The "warns" half of the warn+fallback contract is unverified by the smoke.

CHK-002:adversarial:1: intent claims the smoke writes an audit-config.json where parallelGate has extra unknown keys alongside valid ones and verifies valid keys are still applied. The smoke file has no assertion covering this scenario whatsoever — no tmpProject call with extra keys, no check for unknown-key tolerance. The 28 assertions account for all the checks in the smoke and none correspond to this intent. Evidence is false coverage.

CHK-002:adversarial:0: intent claims the smoke writes a temp audit-config.json with parallelGate set to null and verifies resolveAuditConfig returns profile defaults without throwing. The smoke only tests resolveParallelGate(null, PD) directly at the unit level (line 53); there is no tmpProject call with {parallelGate:null} feeding into resolveAuditConfig. The integration path from JSON config containing null parallelGate through the full resolveAuditConfig pipeline is not covered.

CHK-002:happy:3 (priority=must, type=cli): intent requires mode:off proven via the resolveAuditConfig integration path (proves the reversible escape hatch works in the integrated path), but no tmpProject({parallelGate:{mode:off}}) + resolveAuditConfig call exists in the 39-assertion smoke. Line 79 of parallel-gate-config-smoke.ts calls resolveParallelGate directly (unit path), which satisfies CHK-001:happy:4 but not this integration-level cli intent. The smoke has no resolveAuditConfig(..., tmpProject({parallelGate:{mode:'off'}})) assertion.

CHK-001:edge:1 (priority=should): intent specifies resolveParallelGate({maxConcurrentReview:0}, balancedDefault) returning maxConcurrentReview=3 (balanced profile default), but the smoke at line 98 calls resolveParallelGate({maxConcurrentReview:0}, LIGHT) and asserts result === 2 (light profile default). Profile name and expected fallback value both differ from the intent. The fallback behaviour is proven but not against the named profile. Similarly CHK-001:edge:2 (priority=should): intent says resolveParallelGate({maxConcurrentReview:-1}, balancedDefault) but line 99 uses LIGHT asserting 2; and CHK-001:edge:4 (priority=should): intent says broadGlobBlocks:'yes' against balancedDefault but line 112 uses LIGHT. And CHK-001:adversarial:3 (priority=should): intent says all-wrong-types against balancedDefault but line 121-124 uses STRICT asserting the strict sub-field defaults (4, true). In all four cases the behaviour is tested but with a different named profile than the intent specifies.

CHK-002:edge:1 (priority=should, type=cli) and CHK-002:edge:2 (priority=should, type=cli): both intents require the sub-field guards proven through the resolveAuditConfig integration path (via a tmpProject config file). CHK-002:edge:1 asks for non-integer maxConcurrentReview falling back via the integrated path; CHK-002:edge:2 asks for non-boolean broadGlobBlocks falling back via the integrated path. The smoke exercises both guards only through direct resolveParallelGate calls (lines 98-115), which satisfies the CHK-001 unit intents but not the CHK-002 cli/integration intents. No tmpProject({parallelGate:{maxConcurrentReview:2.5}}) or tmpProject({parallelGate:{broadGlobBlocks:'yes'}}) resolveAuditConfig call exists in the smoke.

CHK-001 userSees is empty — the checklist item defines what the implementer builds but does not describe the observable outcome (the user-visible contract): what does a caller of resolveParallelGate or resolveAuditConfig actually see? Missing userSees means behavioral correctness cannot be formally verified against a stated claim. Fill in userSees describing the resolved ParallelGateConfig values returned for each scenario (correct profile defaults, fallback to advise on bad mode, fallback to profile default on bad maxConcurrentReview/broadGlobBlocks, copy not reference on null input).

CHK-002 userSees is empty — the checklist item describes the test structure (hermetic smoke) but does not declare what the user/operator sees when the smoke passes or fails: no stated output format (count of assertions, exit code, printed message). Without userSees the reviewer cannot verify that the smoke output matches what is claimed. Fill in userSees with the expected output line (e.g., "parallel-gate-config smoke passed: N assertions" printed to stdout, process exits 0; on failure, an error message is printed and process exits 1).

CHK-002:edge:0 (priority must): the intent requires proving warn emission in the integrated resolveAuditConfig path, not just the unit helper. Smoke line 172 checks only .mode === advise via resolveAuditConfig but never wraps the call with captureWarn. The unit-level tests (CHK-001:edge:0, lines 85-87) do capture and assert the warn correctly. CHK-002:edge:0 explicitly calls out proves the warn+fallback path in the integrated smoke, not just the unit helper — the warns half is absent in the integration block. Same deficiency applies to the should-priority integration assertions for maxConcurrentReview (line 180) and broadGlobBlocks (line 184): all three integration-path invalid-value cases are value-only with no captureWarn wrapper.

resolveParallelGate uses 'key in r' which traverses the prototype chain: an Object.create({mode:'block',...})-shaped raw (no own keys) silently overrides profile defaults to block with NO warn, violating the absent-key-keeps-profile-default invariant. Fix: Object.hasOwn for all 3 subfields.
findings.resolvedReason: audit-config.ts: presence now tested with Object.hasOwn(r,'mode'|'maxConcurrentReview'|'broadGlobBlocks') — inherited/prototype-shaped sub-fields are treated as absent. Smoke 8c (Object.create with mode:'block' -> LIGHT kept, no warn) and 8c-bis (__proto__-keyed JSON -> own mode absent, no Object.prototype pollution) prove it. build+validate green, 72 assertions.

findings.desc: JSON.stringify in the warn message throws on BigInt / circular / throwing-toJSON values, so a present-but-invalid subfield crashes resolveParallelGate instead of warn+fallback (lines 93/105/116). Fix: route through a non-throwing describeInvalid formatter.
findings.resolvedReason: audit-config.ts: added describeInvalidValue (bigint-first, JSON.stringify in try/catch, Object.prototype.toString fallback) used in all 3 warn messages — present-but-invalid never throws. Smoke 8d (bigint mode/max, circular mode, throwing-toJSON broadGlobBlocks) all warn+fall-back without crashing.

findings.desc: F-018: the resolveAuditConfig config-file integration invalid cases (lines 172/180/184) assert the fallback VALUE but not warn emission; a silent-fallback regression in the I/O path would pass. Fix: wrap in captureWarn and assert the warn key.
findings.resolvedReason: parallel-gate-config-smoke.ts: integration cases 13/13c/13d now wrap resolveAuditConfig in captureWarn and assert the warn key (mode/maxConcurrentReview/broadGlobBlocks); 13b asserts valid mode 'off' does NOT warn. Integration-path silent-fallback regression is now caught. 72 assertions, validate green.

findings.desc: describeInvalidValue not fully total: the catch fallback Object.prototype.toString.call(value) reads Symbol.toStringTag, which throws for a revoked Proxy or an object with a throwing @@toStringTag getter — so resolveParallelGate still crashes instead of warn+fallback. Fix: nest the fallback in its own try/catch returning a constant <unserializable>; add a revoked-Proxy + throwing-toStringTag smoke case.
findings.resolvedReason: describeInvalidValue catch fallback now nests Object.prototype.toString.call in its own try/catch returning '<unserializable>' — every branch (bigint / JSON.stringify / toString / constant) is total. Smoke 8d-bis adds a revoked-Proxy mode case and a throwing-@@toStringTag max case: both warn+fall-back without crashing. 76 assertions, validate green.

findings.desc: resolveParallelGate outer catch reason rendering 'err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)' can itself throw: a hostile Proxy raw whose getOwnPropertyDescriptor trap THROWS a revoked Proxy makes both 'instanceof' ([[GetPrototypeOf]]) and String(err) (ToPrimitive) throw, escaping the never-throw contract. Fix: render the caught value with describeInvalidValue(err) (the total primitive) so every untrusted-input rendering uses the same total path; add a hostile-throwing-trap smoke case.
findings.resolvedReason: resolveParallelGate outer catch now renders err via describeInvalidValue(err) instead of 'instanceof'/String — the same total primitive used for per-field warns. No instanceof/String/toString on untrusted input remains anywhere, so the catch is itself total and the function is provably total for ALL inputs. Smoke 8d-quater: a hostile Proxy raw whose getOwnPropertyDescriptor trap throws a revoked Proxy -> balanced default, warns, no crash. 80 assertions, validate green.

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: audit-config.ts:250 uses 'as ParallelGateConfig' to strip undefined from profileDefaults.parallelGate, but the idiomatic form is the non-null assertion operator (!) which only removes undefined. The comment says non-null assertion but the code uses a full type cast, which is slightly misleading and weaker — a future shape mismatch would also be silenced.
findings.resolvedReason: audit-config.ts:252 changed 'profileDefaults.parallelGate as ParallelGateConfig' to the narrower non-null assertion 'profileDefaults.parallelGate!' — strips only undefined, preserves shape checking. profileDefaults.parallelGate is set unconditionally above so it is sound. build green.

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: audit-config.ts:108-128 — the outer try/catch in resolveParallelGate catches everything readParallelGateFields throws, including hypothetical future TypeError from a coding mistake (wrong variable access). The warn message 'could not be introspected' would look like a config issue rather than a code bug. Currently not a real risk (readParallelGateFields only uses typeof checks that don't throw on JSON values, and TS catches shape errors at compile time), but worth noting for future maintainers as the function grows.
findings.resolvedReason: The broad outer try/catch is deliberate: the function's contract is never-throw for the PLAN->DEV gate, which requires catching ANY introspection failure. readParallelGateFields uses only non-throwing ops (typeof/Number.isInteger/boolean compare/Object.hasOwn) on JSON values, so the only way to introduce a throw is a coding error, which TypeScript catches at compile time — no reachable runtime logic bug is masked. The JSDoc + inline comment explicitly flag the path as defense-in-depth. Accepted as a documented, intentional tradeoff.

findings.desc: mode and broadGlobBlocks are read twice (guard + assign), so a hostile getter/Proxy could return a valid value for the guard and a different invalid value for the assignment (TOCTOU), yielding an invalid ParallelGateConfig without throwing. Unreachable from JSON.parse but inconsistent with maxConcurrentReview which reads once. Fix: read each field into a const before validating.
findings.resolvedReason: mode and broadGlobBlocks now read once into a const before validate+assign (matching maxConcurrentReview), closing the hostile-getter guard/assign TOCTOU. Smoke 8e: a flaky getter returning valid-then-invalid is read once so the stored value is always the guarded one (this test fails under the old double-read). 82 assertions, validate green.
